q: Who plays Kevin McCallister in Home Alone (1990)?
fact: Culkin was 10 years old when the film opened in November 1990.

q: Who plays Buddy the Elf in Elf (2003)?
fact: Buddy was raised at the North Pole after crawling into Santa's sack as a baby.

q: In Elf, which department store does Buddy visit to meet Santa?
fact: Gimbels was a real New York rival of Macy's that closed in 1986.

q: What is the name of the town in It's a Wonderful Life?
fact: In George's nightmare vision, the town becomes Pottersville.

q: What is the angel Clarence's surname in It's a Wonderful Life?
fact: Clarence is an Angel Second Class, still hoping to earn his wings.

q: What gift does Ralphie want most in A Christmas Story (1983)?
fact: Nearly every adult warns him he will shoot his eye out.

q: What prize does 'The Old Man' win in A Christmas Story?
fact: He proudly displays it in the front window until it is accidentally broken.

q: In the 1966 Grinch special, what happens to the Grinch's small heart?
fact: Chuck Jones directed it, and Boris Karloff narrated and voiced the Grinch.

q: In Rudolph (1964), what job does the elf Hermey want?
fact: Hermey would rather fix teeth than make toys, so he leaves with Rudolph.

q: Which singer voiced Sam the Snowman in Rudolph (1964)?
fact: Ives also sang 'A Holly Jolly Christmas' in the special.

q: In A Charlie Brown Christmas, what kind of tree does Charlie Brown pick?
fact: The special first aired on CBS in December 1965, with Linus explaining Christmas.

q: Who plays the train conductor in The Polar Express (2004)?
fact: Hanks played several roles in the film using motion capture.

q: In The Polar Express, what does the boy choose as his gift from Santa?
fact: The film is based on Chris Van Allsburg's 1985 picture book.

q: In Miracle on 34th Street (1947), where does Kris Kringle work as Santa?
fact: The opening scenes were filmed at the real Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

q: The Nutcracker ballet is based on a tale by which author?
fact: The ballet premiered in St. Petersburg in December 1892, with music by Tchaikovsky.

q: Who is the miserly main character of Dickens' A Christmas Carol?
fact: Dickens published the story in December 1843.

q: What is the name of Bob Cratchit's youngest son in A Christmas Carol?
fact: Fred is actually Scrooge's cheerful nephew, not a Cratchit.

q: Silent Night was first performed in 1818 in which country?
fact: Priest Joseph Mohr wrote the words and teacher Franz Gruber the melody.

q: Who wrote the song White Christmas?
fact: Bing Crosby's recording is widely cited as the best-selling single of all time.

q: Who composed the music for O Holy Night (1847)?
fact: Adam, who also wrote the ballet Giselle, set a French poem by Placide Cappeau.

q: Who sang the 1994 hit All I Want for Christmas Is You?
fact: It first hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in December 2019.

q: Which singing cowboy made Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer a hit in 1949?
fact: Rudolph was created in 1939 by Robert L. May for Montgomery Ward.

q: In 1965, astronauts reportedly played Jingle Bells where?
fact: The Gemini 6 crew used a tiny harmonica and sleigh bells.

q: Let It Snow was written in a July heat wave. Who composed the music?
fact: Styne and lyricist Sammy Cahn wrote it in 1945, and it never mentions Christmas.

q: Carol of the Bells is based on a folk chant from which country?
fact: Mykola Leontovych arranged the Ukrainian New Year chant Shchedryk starting in 1914.

q: Who recorded Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree at age 13?
fact: Recorded in 1958, it hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in December 2023.

q: Which pop group released Last Christmas in 1984?
fact: George Michael wrote and produced it and played nearly every instrument himself.

q: Who wrote the lyrics of Joy to the World?
fact: Watts based it on Psalm 98 and published it in 1719.

q: Who wrote the words to Hark! The Herald Angels Sing?
fact: Its tune was later adapted from music by Felix Mendelssohn.

q: Which two musicians wrote Do They Know It's Christmas? in 1984?
fact: The Band Aid charity single raised money for famine relief in Ethiopia.

q: Which singer made The Christmas Song (chestnuts roasting) a hit in 1946?
fact: Mel Torme and Bob Wells wrote it in 1945 during a hot summer.

q: Feliz Navidad was a 1970 hit for which singer?
fact: Feliciano wrote it in 1970, mixing Spanish and English verses.

q: The Little Drummer Boy was first published in 1941 under what title?
fact: American composer Katherine K. Davis adapted it from a Czech carol.

q: John Lennon and Yoko Ono released which Christmas song in 1971?
fact: It grew out of their 1969 'War Is Over' billboard campaign.

q: Frankincense comes from an Old French phrase meaning what?
fact: The resin comes from Boswellia trees and was one of the Magi's gifts.

q: The X in Xmas comes from which alphabet?
fact: X is the Greek letter chi, the first letter of 'Christos', or Christ.

q: How do you say Merry Christmas in Spanish?
fact: Italian is Buon Natale, and Portuguese is Feliz Natal.

q: Which language says 'Frohe Weihnachten' for Merry Christmas?
fact: Weihnachten roughly means 'hallowed nights'.

q: Mele Kalikimaka means Merry Christmas in which language?
fact: Hawaiian has no r or s sound, so Merry Christmas became Mele Kalikimaka.

q: Wassail comes from Old English words meaning roughly what?
fact: Wassailers also toasted apple orchards in winter to bless the next harvest.

q: The word Noel comes from a Latin word meaning what?
fact: Noel came into English from Old French, from Latin natalis.

q: Santa Claus's name comes from the Dutch name for which saint?
fact: Sinterklaas is the Dutch form, and Dutch settlers brought it to New York.

q: Yule was originally a midwinter festival of which people?
fact: It later blended into Christmas, which is why we still say Yuletide and Yule log.

q: The poinsettia is named after Joel Poinsett, a U.S. envoy to where?
fact: He brought the plant from Mexico to the United States in the 1820s.

q: Donner and Blitzen are German for what?
fact: In the original 1823 poem the pair was spelled Dunder and Blixem.

q: The word Christmas comes from Old English for Christ's what?
fact: Old English 'Cristes maesse' meant Christ's mass, a church service.

q: Joyeux Noel is how you say Merry Christmas in which language?
fact: Noel has the same Latin root as the Italian word Natale.

q: The word tinsel comes from an Old French word meaning what?
fact: Real tinsel was once made from thin strips of silver.

q: Which language says 'Nollaig Shona' for Merry Christmas?
fact: Welsh is Nadolig Llawen, and Scots Gaelic is Nollaig Chridheil.

q: Before it meant a song, the word carol first meant what?
fact: Medieval 'carole' dances were circle dances with singing, later shifting to the songs alone.

q: Advent comes from a Latin word meaning what?
fact: Advent counts down the four Sundays before Christmas, often with a candle wreath.

q: Which furry red toy giggled when squeezed and was the must-have gift of 1996?
fact: Made by Tyco, it sold out fast and resale prices soared far above retail.

q: Cabbage Patch Kid shortages caused shopping frenzies in which year?
fact: Coleco's dolls came with adoption papers, so each one could be 'adopted'.

q: The 1998 hit toy Furby spoke its own language called what?
fact: Furbies start out speaking Furbish and mix in English the longer you play.

q: In The Twelve Days of Christmas, what comes on the fifth day?
fact: The song was first printed in England in 1780.

q: Counting every repeat, how many gifts total in The Twelve Days of Christmas?
fact: That is one gift for every day of the year except one.

q: Which gifts did the three wise men bring?
fact: The Gospel of Matthew lists the gifts but never says there were three men.

q: The teddy bear was named after which U.S. president?
fact: A 1902 cartoon of him refusing to shoot a bear cub inspired the toy.

q: LEGO bricks were invented in which country?
fact: The name comes from the Danish words 'leg godt', meaning 'play well'.

q: In what year did the Barbie doll debut?
fact: Ruth Handler named her after her daughter, Barbara.

q: Rubik's Cube was invented in 1974 in which country?
fact: Ernő Rubik, an architecture professor, first called it the Magic Cube.

q: Which toy 'walks' down stairs, flipping end over end?
fact: Naval engineer Richard James stumbled on the idea, and it hit stores in 1945.

q: Which toy has you draw with two knobs on a gray screen?
fact: French inventor Andre Cassagnes created it, and Ohio Art began selling it in 1960.

q: Play-Doh was first sold as a cleaner for what?
fact: Kutol's wallpaper cleaner was reborn as a modeling toy in the 1950s.

q: Which Mattel toy cars first rolled out in 1968?
fact: Mattel built them to rival Matchbox, the small British die-cast cars.

q: Which company began selling Monopoly in 1935?
fact: An earlier game, The Landlord's Game by Lizzie Magie, was patented in 1904.

q: In The Twelve Days of Christmas, which bird sits in a pear tree?
fact: The twelve days run from Christmas Day to January 5, ending on Twelfth Night.

q: How many turtle doves are in The Twelve Days of Christmas?
fact: Three French hens come next, then four calling birds.

q: Why are snowflakes so often six-sided?
fact: Each flake's branches grow differently, so shapes vary even though all are six-fold.

q: Who first photographed a single snowflake, in 1885?
fact: Bentley, a Vermont farmer, photographed over 5,000 snow crystals in his lifetime.

q: Why does snow look white?
fact: Ice itself is clear, but light bouncing off many tiny crystals mixes to look white.

q: The winter solstice is the Northern Hemisphere's what?
fact: It falls on December 21 or 22 in the Northern Hemisphere.

q: What causes Earth's seasons?
fact: Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January, during Northern winter.

q: When it is Christmas in Australia, what season is it?
fact: In December the Southern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun.

q: On the December solstice, where is the Sun directly overhead at noon?
fact: That line sits about 23.4 degrees south of the equator.

q: What is a house built from blocks of snow called?
fact: Igloo comes from the Inuit word 'iglu', meaning house.

q: At what temperature does water freeze on the Fahrenheit scale?
fact: That is 0 degrees on the Celsius scale.

q: Where was Earth's coldest recorded temperature measured?
fact: Vostok Station in Antarctica recorded about minus 89 degrees C in 1983.

q: Solstice comes from Latin words meaning the Sun does what?
fact: The Sun's rise and set points seem to pause before reversing direction.

q: Mount Baker, WA set a record 1,140 inches of snow in a season. How many feet?
fact: That 1998-99 season is recognized as the world record for one season.

q: What are snowflakes made of?
fact: They form when water vapor freezes onto a tiny speck of dust high in the clouds.

q: What are the hanging spikes of ice on a roof edge called?
fact: They form when melting water drips and refreezes, layer by layer.

q: The U.S. National Weather Service says a blizzard needs wind of at least how many mph?
fact: It also needs visibility under a quarter mile for three hours or more.

q: On average, 10 inches of fresh snow melts into about how much water?
fact: That 10 to 1 ratio varies, since fluffy powder holds less water than wet snow.

q: Puritan-run Massachusetts began fining Christmas celebrations in which year?
fact: The law fined observers five shillings and was repealed in 1681.

q: Which organization tracks Santa's flight each Christmas Eve?
fact: It began in 1955 when a misprinted store ad sent kids' calls to a military line.

q: The first commercial Christmas card was sent in 1843 in which country?
fact: Sir Henry Cole commissioned it, and about 1,000 copies were printed.

q: Christmas Island in the Indian Ocean was named for what date of its sighting?
fact: Captain William Mynors named it in 1643, and Australia governs it today.

q: In which country is a KFC meal a popular Christmas tradition?
fact: A 1974 marketing campaign called 'Kentucky for Christmas' started the trend.

q: London's Trafalgar Square tree is a yearly thank-you gift from which country?
fact: Norway has sent it since 1947 to thank Britain for its help in World War II.

q: In the 1930s, ads from which drink company popularized Santa's red-suited look?
fact: Artist Haddon Sundblom painted the jolly Santa ads starting in 1931.

q: Which New York landmark puts up a famous giant tree each December?
fact: The tradition began in 1931, when construction workers set up a small tree.

q: In which country do families watch Donald Duck at 3 p.m. on Christmas Eve?
fact: The show 'Kalle Anka' has aired on Swedish TV on Christmas Eve since 1959.

q: In 1647, England's Puritan-led Parliament did what to Christmas?
fact: Festivities returned when the monarchy was restored in 1660.

q: Which U.S. state first made Christmas a legal holiday, in 1836?
fact: Congress made Christmas a federal holiday on June 26, 1870.

q: The 1914 Christmas Truce, with shared carols, took place in which war?
fact: It is remembered for carols and some informal soccer games in no man's land.

q: Santa Claus Village, right on the Arctic Circle, is in which country?
fact: It is in Rovaniemi, and a line across the village marks the Arctic Circle.

q: Which U.S. state has a town named Santa Claus that gets letters for Santa?
fact: Volunteer 'elves' there answer thousands of letters to Santa each year.

q: In Iceland, what is it a tradition to give and read on Christmas Eve?
fact: Called the 'Christmas Book Flood', it sees most new Icelandic books released each fall.

q: Which royal helped popularize the Christmas tree in Britain in the 1840s?
fact: An 1848 engraving of the royal family by a tree sparked a craze, even in America.
